138. White Night Tower Keeper (2)
"Runcandel and Kinzelo have also infiltrated the Second Magic Tower. Is that all?"
The white-haired old man replied calmly to the urgent report from the messengers who had just come through the teleportation gate.
He was Kelliark Gipple, the strongest archmage of this era and the leader of the world's number one organization.
At the time when the warehouse was attacked, he had been spending time on the uninhabited island in the western sea where Veradin's villa was located.

During the "Western Sea Battle" waged by Talaris, Misha, Octavia, and the Phantom Unit, the uninhabited island had been completely turned to dust and disappeared, but now the island, along with the villa and all the belongings Veradin had used, had been perfectly restored.
"Moreover, Miss Sandra has deployed all the forces of the Second Magic Tower. If you give the order, I will return and immediately send the Drakka's magicians to the Second Magic Tower."
Kelliark flipped through the pages of a book silently for a while. Then, he seemed to find something interesting, used his magic to underline it, and smiled.
"Don't be too surprised by fate."
The messengers were feeling anxious as they waited for Kelliark to speak. Time was of the essence.
However, Kelliark had anticipated from the beginning that an external force would be able to attack both the warehouse and the Second Magic Tower.
He just wondered if there was any need for special preparations.
'Hedo.'
It was because that man was in the White Night Tower.
'This time will be an opportunity to test him again.'
Since Hedo became a member of the Gipple, Kelliark had wanted to test him continuously.
It was still difficult to determine whether Hedo was truly loyal to the Gipple.

"Send support troops only to the warehouse. Furthermore, since the capabilities of external forces have already been confirmed, further resource losses are meaningless. Protect as many resources as possible."
"Yes, sir!"
The messengers bowed in unison and stepped back into the darkness.
Kelliark gazed out at the sea beyond, recalling the moment he first met Hedo long ago.
Kruk...!
Suddenly, Murakan clutched his head with both hands. It was as if an unbearable headache was coming, and his waist buckled.

Jin and the Runcandels quickly surrounded Murakan and spread a protective shield. Although they had anticipated it since Hedo's appearance, the tension after actually receiving the sword strike was incomparable to the battle's beginning.
Showing such a gap in front of a transcendent warrior like Hedo was, without a doubt, a fatal mistake.
Fortunately, he did not take advantage of Murakan's vulnerability.
It wasn't that he couldn't do it. Although he didn't show it, Hedo was somewhat intrigued by what Murakan had just said.

'It's the first time I've seen someone speak as if they know about the Bale. Even the leader of the Ciron family and the lord of the continent seemed to have no idea about the identity of this sword.'
Bale.
On the sword spirit of the special longsword Hedo had obtained by chance long ago, such a word was engraved in small letters.
It was unclear whether it was the name of the sword, the name of the blacksmith who made the sword, or the name of the person who used the sword.
In his youth, when he was searching for the ultimate swordsmanship against the wave of martial arts, he was curious about the identity of the longsword.
However, Hedo soon concluded that the Bale was the name of the sword, as it seemed to have little meaning to know its identity.
The reason Hedo didn't take advantage of Murakan's crumbling posture was that he wanted him to talk about the Bale.
It was also a matter of confidence.

Even if he could afford this much, the outcome would not change. The reason Kelliark said that Gipple would not send reinforcements to the Second Magic Tower was the same. Kelliark knew he was here, so it must have been.
"Murakan."
Jin called in a low voice and checked Murakan's condition. He looked very distressed and confused.
'Like the day I first met Kinzelo's leader in the old Otelium, when he talked about Temar. I don't know why, but is Hedo's sword stimulating Murakan's chaotic memory...?'
Unlike Jin, who knew that Murakan's memory was incomplete and that such a problem could arise when a conflict occurred because of it.
The other Runcandels didn't know the reason. It was only embarrassing that the guardian of the family suddenly fell into a panic in a desperate situation.
"Krrrr!"
Murakan groaned again.
1 second, 2 seconds, 3 seconds....
As a Runcandel, they felt the sense of crisis multiply with each passing second.
If Murakan couldn't fight properly, the Runcandels would most likely be captured or annihilated.
Jin made a decision.
'Like that time, this has to work. Like the day I first met Kinzelo's leader, when he babbled nonsense!'
With a loud noise, a fierce impact rang out in the quiet hall.
Jin literally threw his fist at Murakan's head with all his strength and at the fastest possible speed.
It was an action based on Jin's experience, but others who didn't know the situation could only think that Jin was crazy.
Murakan, who was hit so hard in the back of the head, stood still for a while like a tree. He seemed to have turned to stone.
However, his head was slightly bent in the direction where Jin had struck him with his fist.
"Youngest, what is this?"
Diphus managed to steady his trembling voice and asked.
"Surely, Murakan isn't dead, is he?" For a moment, that thought crossed their minds.
Of course, that wouldn't be the case, but the complete lack of movement made it seem plausible.
The angle of the twisted neck was somewhat awkward… Taking a full-force blow from Jin while being defenseless was quite dangerous.
"Ugh… It hurts like hell."
Fortunately for the Runcandels, after what seemed like an eternity, Murakan finally spoke in an annoyed tone.
"Are you back to your senses?"
"It seems I... hmm… had a brief relapse of my illness? Anyway, kid, how could you hit me like that?"
Crack! Snap! Murakan twisted his head and loosened his neck joints while continuing to speak.
"My appearance is ruined! How could you?! Huh? Oh…"
Murakan, who had been speaking confidently, suddenly wavered and lost his balance.

Although his mind had returned, Jin had overlooked one fact. When he used the same shock treatment in the old Oterium, Jin was exhausted, but now he was full of energy. He had become much stronger since then.

"Damn, kid. You should have controlled your strength! My skull is ringing and the world is spinning. But what's with that sword? It seems to have a close connection with me. Whenever I try to remember, it feels like my head is going to explode."
As curious as he was, he needed to focus on the fight for now in order to save the contractor.
"It doesn't seem like that pretty boy would lie or use shallow tricks. He clearly said that no reinforcements would come."
In that case, it was time to put forth their full effort.
"Kid."
"Yes."
"Transform into your true form. If that pretty boy turns out to be a petty liar and reinforcements arrive, leave me and escape. Got it?"
Jin nodded heavily.
He didn't actually intend to leave Murakan and run away, but for now, it was better to agree. After all, whether reinforcements came or not, there was no hope without Murakan giving his all.
"…There are parts I don't quite understand, but I'll accept that you needed time for planning. Do I need to wait any longer?"
Having hoped that Murakan would talk about his sword, Hedo concluded that there was no need for further patience.

"Heh, you're undoubtedly the best I've seen in this era. But I am Murakan. My prestige may have faded after a thousand years and your master's family's long-standing schemes, but Murakan is still Murakan."
Hooong…!
As Murakan finished speaking, his shadow grew larger.
Soon, he dispersed into black smoke and transformed into the true form of a black dragon, darkly fluttering his pair of wings.
Kaaaah!
Following the sharp and gloomy roar, Hedo adjusted his glasses with a refined gesture.
"I'll be looking forward to it."
A sudden black curtain spread, staining the ceiling dark. Inside it, the swirling energies viciously rotated like the pupils of giants, all of them aimed at Hedo.
Dark flames formed around the energy-wrapped Bradamante, and dazzling auras surged from Joshua, Diphus, and Jane's swords.
The spectral troops also gathered magical power, and Hedo took a deep breath.
The intensifying energies of the superhumans made the air ripple as if it would tear, and the entire tower vibrated uncomfortably.
The expansion just before the clash.
Hedo was the first to break that precarious phenomenon.
"Hmm!"
Hedo's restrained swordsmanship pierced through the chaotic landscape of mixed energies, auras, and magic power.
It was a simple thrust.
It was also a perfect thrust. His longsword penetrated the center of the tangled energies diagonally.
His target was Murakan.

With the massive body of the dragon, there was no way to evade the speed and distance. Counterattacking while avoiding a fatal blow or neutralizing it with equal or greater power was usually the only option a dragon could choose.
However, at that moment, Murakan turned into black smoke again and dispersed his body to avoid Hedo's sword strike.
Simultaneously, he counterattacked with dozens of energy whirlwinds.
'Tsk!'
It wasn't that he didn't suffer any damage. Hedo's accomplished swordsmanship struck and injured the particles of Murakan's scattered smoke form.

Hedo also showed a form that evaded the attack using a stepping technique instead of taking it with his body. Not only did Murakan's attack fall short, but the venomous strikes from the Runcandels would follow as well.
Also, as a result of Murakan avoiding Hedo's thrust.
Hedo's sharp sword strike, unobstructed by planned defenses and resistance, swooped down on the spectral troops who were positioned behind the Runcandels.
Thus, for the spectral troops, it was an extremely frustrating and outrageous situation that made them feel like they would go mad.
